title: Unauthorized location data sharing
description: Child's device shares live GPS coordinates without explicit consent or awareness of the extent of location tracking
assumptions: Child may not understand the implications of continuous location tracking

title: Personal identification through location data
description: GPS coordinates can be used to identify and track the child's movements and habits
assumptions: Location data is personally identifiable information

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted over network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties
assumptions: Data is transmitted over potentially insecure channels

title: Metadata linking parties
description: Data flow metadata (timing, frequency, source/destination) can be used to link and identify the child and app
assumptions: Metadata is collected and analyzed by third parties

title: Location data storage without proper security
description: Backend may store location data without adequate encryption or access controls
assumptions: Data storage security is not guaranteed

title: Unintended consequences of location tracking
description: Continuous location tracking may lead to unintended profiling or surveillance of the child
assumptions: Location data may be used for purposes beyond the original intent

title: Location History Data Disclosure
description: Personal location data is stored in the Location History Store, creating a persistent record that could be accessed by unauthorized parties or used for tracking users across time. This explicit disclosure of personal data violates the minimality principle by retaining location history beyond what may be strictly necessary.
assumptions: Location data is considered personal data under applicable privacy regulations

title: Location Data Linkability
description: Location pings in transit contain identifying information that could be used to link or identify individuals. The metadata about when and where location data is transmitted could be used to profile or track user behavior patterns.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient identifying information to link to specific individuals

title: Location Data Confidentiality
description: Location history stored in the data store may be accessible by unauthorized parties if access controls are not properly implemented. This could lead to unauthorized profiling, surveillance, or misuse of personal location information.
assumptions: Data store access controls may not be sufficient to prevent unauthorized access

title: Explicit location data disclosure to third-party process
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) intentionally shares location pings with Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2). If P2 is a third-party service or if the data sharing exceeds what is strictly required for geofencing functionality, this represents an explicit data disclosure that may violate minimality principles.
assumptions: P2 may be a third-party service or the data sharing may exceed necessary scope for geofencing
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: If P2 is an internal system and the data sharing is strictly required for geofencing, this may be an intentional design rather than a threat.

title: Location data used for cross-session user linking
description: Location pings in transit between P1 and P2 may contain metadata or patterns that can be used to link user sessions, infer user identity across different contexts, or build profiles of user movement patterns.
assumptions: Location data may contain identifiers or be correlated across sessions
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: Depends on whether location data includes user identifiers and whether P2 correlates data across sessions.

title: Inference of user behavior from location data
description: Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) processes location pings to determine zone entry/exit, which may enable inference of user behavior patterns, habits, or sensitive activities based on location data.
assumptions: Location data enables inference of user behavior patterns
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: Severity depends on the sensitivity of the geofenced zones and whether the inferred behavior is considered sensitive.

title: Location data shared from DataStore
description: Zone definitions containing home, school, and friend's house locations are being shared from the DataStore, exposing sensitive location information.

title: Identification data shared from DataStore
description: Zone definitions can be used to identify users and their personal habits and routines, enabling profiling of user behavior patterns.

title: Location data in transit
description: Location-based zone definitions are transmitted in transit, potentially exposing location information to interception or unauthorized access.

title: Data not handled appropriately at destination
description: The Geofencing Engine may not be storing or handling zone definitions in a privacy-compliant manner, potentially leading to unauthorized access or improper retention.

title: Location data shared without consent
description: Geofencing Engine shares location-based arrival/departure notifications to external parent entity without explicit consent or appropriate consent management
assumptions: Assumes location data is being shared without documented consent framework

title: Flow metadata enables party linking
description: Data in transit contains metadata about parties (sender/receiver) that could be used to link or identify individuals across multiple flows
assumptions: Assumes metadata about data flow participants is transmitted

title: Location data stored without purpose limitation
description: Parent entity receives location notifications and may store/process them without clear purpose limitation or retention policy
assumptions: Assumes parent entity stores the received notifications

title: Unintended location tracking consequences
description: Sharing geofencing data may lead to unintended tracking or profiling of individuals based on their movement patterns
assumptions: Assumes location data could be used for profiling or tracking

title: Lawfulness of data collection
description: Parent sharing child's sensitive profile data (name, DOB, school) and geofence zones may lack clear legal basis or parental consent documentation
assumptions: Assumes GDPR/CCPA compliance requirements apply to child data collection

title: Appropriateness of information shared
description: Parent may share more child information than necessary for account registration and profile creation
assumptions: Assumes minimal data sharing principle should apply

title: Necessity of data collection
description: School information and geofence zones may not be necessary for basic account registration
assumptions: Assumes account creation should be minimal

title: Unintended interception of child data
description: Sensitive child profile data and geofence information transmitted in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over network

title: Data minimization at destination
description: Mobile app backend may store more child data than necessary for intended purposes
assumptions: Assumes data retention policies may exceed minimum requirements

title: Unintended access to child profile
description: Child profile data stored at destination may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems
assumptions: Assumes access controls may be insufficient

title: Location History Data Exposure at Source
description: Location history data is being shared from the DataStore to the Mobile App Backend, potentially exposing sensitive location patterns of users without explicit consent or appropriate safeguards.
assumptions: Location history contains personal movement patterns that could reveal sensitive locations (home, workplace, etc.)

title: User Identification via Location History
description: Location history data can be used to identify and track individual users, potentially enabling profiling and re-identification of users.
assumptions: Location history is unique to individual users and can be linked to specific individuals

title: Location Data in Transit
description: Location history data is transmitted in transit between DataStore and Mobile App Backend, potentially exposing location information to network interceptors.
assumptions: Data transmission may occur over networks that could be monitored or intercepted

title: Unintended Disclosure of Location History
description: The Mobile App Backend may process or store location history in a way that could lead to unintended disclosure to unauthorized parties or in unintended contexts.
assumptions: The backend may have insufficient access controls or data handling procedures

title: Data Integrity Risk During Processing
description: Location history data may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during processing by the Mobile App Backend, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: The backend processing environment may not have adequate integrity controls

title: Parent shares child's location data
description: Parent initiates sharing of child's location data to secondary guardian, which could enable tracking of child's movements and create a persistent record of location history.
assumptions: Parent has access to child's location data and chooses to share it with secondary guardian

title: Parent's identity linked to child's location
description: When parent shares location data, their identity becomes associated with the child's location information, potentially enabling tracking of parent-child relationships.
assumptions: Location data includes or is linked to parent's identity information

title: Location data in transit
description: Child's location data transmitted from parent to mobile app backend is in transit and could be intercepted by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data transmission occurs over network that may not be fully secured

title: Flow metadata links parties
description: Meta-data about the source (parent) and destination (app backend) in the data flow could be used to link or identify the parties involved.
assumptions: Flow metadata includes information about source and destination entities

title: Location data stored and processed
description: Mobile app backend receives and stores child's location data, which could be used for tracking, profiling, or unauthorized access to location history.
assumptions: App backend stores location data and may process it for various purposes

title: Location data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: Mobile app backend may disclose child's location data to unauthorized parties, including secondary guardians who may not have proper authorization.
assumptions: App backend has access controls that may not be properly implemented

title: Location data shared with external guardian
description: Mobile App Backend shares child's live location with Secondary Guardian, creating risk of location tracking and surveillance
assumptions: Assumes location data is shared without proper consent or privacy controls

title: Location data used to identify child
description: Sharing live location enables identification and tracking of the child, potentially violating privacy expectations
assumptions: Assumes location data can be used to uniquely identify the child

title: Location data in transit exposed
description: Live location data transmitted between P1 and EE3 may be intercepted or monitored during transit
assumptions: Assumes data transmission may not be fully encrypted or protected

title: Location data misused by guardian
description: Secondary Guardian may misuse the child's location data for purposes beyond the intended scope
assumptions: Assumes guardian may have access to location data for purposes not authorized by the original sharing

title: Location data used to identify child
description: Secondary Guardian may use location data to identify and track the child, potentially violating privacy expectations
assumptions: Assumes guardian may use location data for identification purposes

title: Linkage via metadata in analytics flow
description: The data flow contains metadata about the parties (user, app, partner) that can be used to link or identify users across different contexts, even if the analytics are aggregated.
assumptions: Assumes metadata is preserved in transit and can be analyzed by third parties.

title: Potential user identification in aggregated analytics
description: The source process may share aggregated analytics that could still be used to identify individual users through re-identification techniques or correlation with other data sources.
assumptions: Assumes aggregation is not perfect and some identifying information may be retained.

title: Unintended data use by advertising partner
description: The destination external entity may use the analytics data for purposes beyond what was intended, such as building user profiles or selling the data to third parties.
assumptions: Assumes the partner has access to the data and may not honor intended use restrictions.

title: Unintended consequences from data sharing
description: The data flow may have unintended consequences, such as enabling the partner to track user behavior across different apps or services.
assumptions: Assumes the partner has access to the data and may use it for purposes beyond the stated funding purpose.

title: Non-repudiation of SOS message
description: The child's SOS/check-in message may not be verifiably attributed to the child, as there is no cryptographic signature or authentication mechanism to prove the message originated from the child.
assumptions: Assumes no digital signature or authentication is used for the manual check-in/SOS message.

title: Data integrity during transmission
description: The location data in the SOS message could be altered or tampered with during transmission between the child and the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network that may be vulnerable to interception or modification.

title: Data confidentiality during transmission
description: The location data and SOS message could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing the child's location to third parties.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network that may be vulnerable to eavesdropping.

title: Data availability failure
description: The mobile app backend may fail to receive or process the SOS message due to system failures, network issues, or service outages, potentially delaying or preventing the parent from receiving critical location information.
assumptions: Assumes the mobile app backend is not always available and may experience failures.
